paper_metadata.title: Implementing the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms for QUBO problems Across Quantum Hardware Platforms: Performance Analysis, Challenges, and Strategies

summary: The paper evaluates standard QAOA and ADAPT‑QAOA for synthetic feature‑selection QUBO problems with 6, 10, and 14 variables using an ideal Qiskit simulator (up to 30 layers, 10,000 shots). ADAPT‑QAOA achieves higher approximation ratios on harder instances (α = 0.6), sometimes approaching the exact solution, but incurs longer runtimes due to mixer selection overhead, and a classical Gurobi QUBO solver scales significantly better in time‑to‑solution. The authors also estimate hardware performance using calibration data from ibm_brisbane and Quantinuum H2, finding superconducting devices faster but trapped‑ion systems lower in error probability.

experiments.description: Ideal-simulator study comparing standard QAOA and ADAPT-QAOA on randomly generated feature-selection QUBO instances of sizes 6, 10, and 14 features, with trade-off parameters alpha=0.2 and alpha=0.6, using up to 30 layers.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: gamma initialized randomly in [0, 2pi]; beta initialized randomly in [0, pi]

problem_formulation.objective_function: f_FS(x) = -(1-alpha) sum_i Q_ii x_i + alpha sum_{i<j} Q_ij x_i x_j
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_C = -(1-alpha) sum_i Q_ii (1-Z_i)/2 + alpha sum_{i<j} Q_ij (1-Z_i)/2 (1-Z_j)/2
